slides.texte_overlay:
Small changes that make
your home feel calmer
Clear one surface completely. The kitchen counter, the desk or the bedside table. One empty, clean surface gives your eyes a place to rest every time you walk in.
Swap bright ceiling lights for lamps in the evening. Warm, low light after sunset tells your brain the day is ending and makes the whole room feel softer.
Give everything a home. Keys in a bowl, chargers in a drawer, shoes by the door. When things have a place, the mess stops piling up and so does the stress.
Add one living plant. Something easy like a snake plant or a pothos. Caring for something green slows you down and makes any room feel more alive.
Make one corner for quiet moments. I do five minutes a day of history, art or science in my reading chair, and it's become the calmest part of my home.
slides.texte_sophia: I do five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app in my reading chair. History, art, science. It's become the calmest corner of my home.

slides.texte_overlay: Open the windows every morning. Ten minutes of fresh air clears the stale feeling from a room and wakes you up better than a second coffee.
Keep screens out of the bedroom. No TV, phone charging in the hall. A room that's only for rest helps your mind switch off as soon as you walk in.
